segments.metaDescription: Non-ingestible pet tech and wellness for responsible breeders: whelping-box monitoring, litter safety, ID and calm handling — plus a Breeder Starter Kit.
segments.heroIntro: From the whelping box to their first homes, PawSense helps responsible breeders monitor, protect and gently socialise every puppy or kitten — with non-ingestible tech and wellness built for busy programmes.
segments.indexBlurb: Whelping monitoring, litter safety and a Breeder Starter Kit for responsible programmes.
segments.whoFor: Hobby and professional dog and cat breeders raising planned litters who want to monitor the whelping box, keep newborns safe and warm, and hand over confident, well-socialised pups and kittens.
segments.why: The first weeks decide temperament and health. Simple monitoring and warmth reduce risk overnight, and early, positive exposure to handling and sound builds the calm, adaptable animals new owners are looking for.

reads.title: Setting up the whelping box
reads.body: Warmth, quiet and a clear line of sight matter most. Position the box away from draughts and foot traffic, keep a warm resting zone the dam can leave, and use a camera so you can check without disturbing her overnight.

reads.title: Early socialisation, week by week
reads.body: Gentle daily handling, varied surfaces and gradually introduced everyday sounds between weeks 3 and 12 build resilience. Keep sessions short and positive, and never overwhelm — the goal is curiosity, not stress.

reads.title: Safe ID for a whole litter
reads.body: Colour-coded collars and a QR ID plan make it easy to track weights and worming per pup, and give new owners an instant ID solution the day they collect.

problems.title: Overnight peace of mind
problems.text: Newborns fade fast if they get cold or separated. Quiet monitoring lets you check the box without disturbing the dam.

problems.title: Warmth without risk
problems.text: A safe, even warm zone supports tiny bodies that can't yet regulate their own temperature.

problems.title: Confident hand-over
problems.text: New owners want ID, records and a calm animal. Give them a head start on day one.

faqs.q: Is the monitoring camera safe near a whelping box?
faqs.a: Yes — it's a non-contact camera placed outside the box so you can watch without disturbing the dam. Keep all cables out of reach as with any electrical device.

segments.metaTitle: Cats & Dogs Together — Multi-Pet Harmony Essentials | PawSense
segments.metaDescription: Help cats and dogs share a home in peace: safe spaces, calm introductions, monitoring and enrichment that reduce conflict and encourage mutual play.
segments.heroIntro: Cats and dogs can be great housemates with the right setup. PawSense helps multi-pet homes create safe spaces, reduce conflict, and encourage the calm curiosity that turns into real companionship.
segments.indexBlurb: Safe spaces, calm introductions, monitoring and enrichment for cats-and-dogs homes.
segments.whoFor: Households sharing life with both cats and dogs — whether introducing a new pet or smoothing an established but tense relationship.
segments.why: Most cat-dog friction comes from resources, space and pace, not personality. Give each pet retreat options, control the introductions, and monitor the flashpoints, and rivalry usually settles into tolerance — often into play.

reads.title: Introducing a cat and dog the right way
reads.body: Go slow: scent-swap first, then barrier meetings, then short supervised sessions. Reward calm, end on a good note, and never force contact — the cat needs an easy exit at all times.

reads.title: Giving the cat safe high ground
reads.body: Cats settle when they can watch from above and retreat when they want. Dog-free resting spots and vertical escape routes prevent most stand-offs.

reads.title: Encouraging safe shared play
reads.body: Parallel play and calm shared routines build tolerance. Keep high-value toys and food separate at first to avoid guarding, and monitor the early sessions.

problems.title: Everyone needs a retreat
problems.text: A cat with safe high ground and a dog with its own rest spot rarely clash.

problems.title: Controlled introductions
problems.text: Slow, positive meetings prevent a bad first impression sticking.

problems.title: Watch the flashpoints
problems.text: Food, doorways and toys cause most spats — monitoring catches them early.

faqs.q: Can cats and dogs really live together happily?
faqs.a: Very often, yes. With safe retreats, slow introductions and monitored early sessions, most cat-dog pairs settle into tolerance and frequently into play.

faqs.q: How do I stop my cat and dog fighting over food?
faqs.a: Feed them separately, keep high-value toys apart at first, and give the cat elevated, dog-free space. Most conflict is about resources, not dislike.
Anywhere from days to several weeks. Go at the more nervous animal's pace, reward calm, and never force contact.
